import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Create a comprehensive figure with multiple subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# Calculate total spending per customer
df['TotalSpending'] = (df['MntWines'] + df['MntFruits'] + df['MntMeatProducts'] + 
                       df['MntFishProducts'] + df['MntSweetProducts'] + df['MntGoldProds'])

# Calculate age
df['Age'] = 2024 - df['Year_Birth']

# 1. Income Distribution (top left)
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
df['Income'].dropna().hist(bins=40, ax=ax1, color='steelblue', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax1.set_xlabel('Income', fontsize=10)
ax1.set_ylabel('Frequency', fontsize=10)
ax1.set_title('Income Distribution', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax1.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# 2. Total Spending by Education (top middle)
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
education_spending = df.groupby('Education')['TotalSpending'].mean().sort_values()
education_spending.plot(kind='barh', ax=ax2, color='coral')
ax2.set_xlabel('Average Total Spending', fontsize=10)
ax2.set_ylabel('Education Level', fontsize=10)
ax2.set_title('Average Spending by Education', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax2.grid(axis='x', alpha=0.3)

# 3. Age vs Total Spending Scatter (top right)
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
scatter = ax3.scatter(df['Age'], df['TotalSpending'], c=df['Income'], 
                     cmap='viridis', alpha=0.5, s=30)
ax3.set_xlabel('Age', fontsize=10)
ax3.set_ylabel('Total Spending', fontsize=10)
ax3.set_title('Age vs Spending (colored by Income)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
cbar = plt.colorbar(scatter, ax=ax3)
cbar.set_label('Income', fontsize=9)
ax3.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 4. Product Category Spending (middle left)
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])
product_cols = ['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 
                'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']
product_spending = df[product_cols].sum().sort_values(ascending=True)
product_labels = ['Wines', 'Fruits', 'Meat', 'Fish', 'Sweets', 'Gold']
colors = plt.cm.Set3(range(len(product_spending)))
product_spending.plot(kind='barh', ax=ax4, color=colors)
ax4.set_yticklabels(product_labels)
ax4.set_xlabel('Total Spending Across All Customers', fontsize=10)
ax4.set_title('Spending by Product Category', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax4.grid(axis='x', alpha=0.3)

# 5. Purchase Channel Distribution (middle middle)
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
channels = ['Web', 'Catalog', 'Store', 'Deals']
channel_data = [df['NumWebPurchases'].sum(), df['NumCatalogPurchases'].sum(),
                df['NumStorePurchases'].sum(), df['NumDealsPurchases'].sum()]
colors_pie = ['#ff9999', '#66b3ff', '#99ff99', '#ffcc99']
wedges, texts, autotexts = ax5.pie(channel_data, labels=channels, autopct='%1.1f%%',
                                     colors=colors_pie, startangle=90)
for autotext in autotexts:
    autotext.set_color('white')
    autotext.set_fontsize(9)
    autotext.set_fontweight('bold')
ax5.set_title('Purchase Channel Distribution', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')

# 6. Marital Status vs Income (middle right)
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
marital_income = df.groupby('Marital_Status')['Income'].median().sort_values()
marital_income.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax6, color='lightseagreen', edgecolor='black')
ax6.set_xlabel('Marital Status', fontsize=10)
ax6.set_ylabel('Median Income', fontsize=10)
ax6.set_title('Median Income by Marital Status', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax6.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
ax6.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# 7. Campaign Response Rate (bottom left)
ax7 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
campaign_cols = ['AcceptedCmp1', 'AcceptedCmp2', 'AcceptedCmp3', 'AcceptedCmp4', 'AcceptedCmp5', 'Response']
campaign_rates = df[campaign_cols].sum() / len(df) * 100
campaign_labels = ['Cmp1', 'Cmp2', 'Cmp3', 'Cmp4', 'Cmp5', 'Last Cmp']
campaign_rates.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax7, color='mediumpurple', edgecolor='black')
ax7.set_xticklabels(campaign_labels, rotation=0)
ax7.set_ylabel('Acceptance Rate (%)', fontsize=10)
ax7.set_title('Campaign Response Rates', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax7.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# 8. Kids at Home vs Spending (bottom middle)
ax8 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 1])
df['TotalKids'] = df['Kidhome'] + df['Teenhome']
kids_spending = df.groupby('TotalKids')['TotalSpending'].mean()
ax8.plot(kids_spending.index, kids_spending.values, marker='o', linewidth=2, 
         markersize=8, color='crimson')
ax8.set_xlabel('Number of Kids at Home', fontsize=10)
ax8.set_ylabel('Average Total Spending', fontsize=10)
ax8.set_title('Impact of Children on Spending', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax8.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 9. Recency Distribution (bottom right)
ax9 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 2])
df['Recency'].hist(bins=30, ax=ax9, color='goldenrod', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax9.set_xlabel('Days Since Last Purchase', fontsize=10)
ax9.set_ylabel('Number of Customers', fontsize=10)
ax9.set_title('Customer Recency Distribution', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax9.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)
ax9.axvline(df['Recency'].median(), color='red', linestyle='--', 
            linewidth=2, label=f"Median: {df['Recency'].median():.0f} days")
ax9.legend(fontsize=9)

# Main title
fig.suptitle('Customer Segmentation Analysis Dashboard', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.995)
